name: Porsche 356 1500 Coupé
description:
Porsche's first production car. Erwin Komenda drew the body; the engine block and much of the suspension began as Volkswagen parts and were reworked from there. Production started at Gmünd in Austria in 1948, where about fifty were built by hand, and moved to Zuffenhausen in Germany in 1950 — the cars from there being the ones now called Pre-A.

This is the 1500 of 1953–55. The bumpers stand clear of the body, the two-piece windscreen has given way to a single pane with a crease down the middle — the Knickscheibe — and the rear lamps are round. The engine is the type 546/2: 1,488 cc, air-cooled flat-four, two Solex 32 PBI carburettors, pushrods and rockers off a single camshaft, 7:1 compression and 55 hp at 4,400 rpm. The 1500 S made 70. Platform chassis, torsion bars front and rear, swing axles behind, worm-and-roller steering, drums all round, four speeds, about 830 kg and just under four metres long.

The 356 A replaced it in 1956, and the 356 itself ran until April 1965, well after the 911 had arrived. Some 76,313 were built in all, of which 7,627 were Gmünd cars and Pre-As.
author: GeroDa74
